$comment: Standing platform test checklist — area ledger. Hand-edited, append-only; validated by scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs (pnpm check:platform-checklist). Authoring rules: docs/qa/platform-checklist/README.md · execution protocol: RUNNER.md.
title: Cross-cutting UX conventions — every write answers, every disabled control explains itself, labels over machine names (console and Studio)

items.title: Every user-initiated write answers visibly — success names what changed, a refusal says why, and a no-op claims nothing
personas: member (non-admin end user) for the record rows

requires: a writable scratch package for the Studio rows — create it from the Studio landing and delete it at teardown; the showcase package itself is read-only in Studio
the organization capability for the Invite User row (a stock showcase boot bootstraps a Default Organization)
an independent read of server truth for every row — a second browser context or the REST API — so a write is never judged by what the UI says about it
knownGaps: FIXED, regression row, expected PASS (objectui#11817): Setup → Users → Invite User toasts 'Invitation sent to EMAIL' — the declared successMessage `Invitation sent to {{ result.email }}` (packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts#invite_user) interpolating the invitee from the action result — while the sys_invitation and sys_email rows are written (QA run #23163 at objectui 1fb1ced36243; pin ObjectView.inviteFeedback-11817.test.tsx)

FIXED, regression rows, expected PASS (QA run #23953 at objectui daeb77fc84dd): Studio Publish gives a success confirmation (objectui#11807); the task grid's 'Save All' toasts '1 row saved' (objectui#12303 fixed for this row); the approval decision's Approve toasted the framework-declared successMessage, read in the approvals drawer that route no longer has (variants[6]) `Approved "{{ result.request.record_title }}"` (packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/sys-approval-request.object.ts), e.g. Approved "EXP-2001" (#23157, closed). Studio's 'Discard draft' toast and its confirm now name the item by its LABEL — QA run #24570 at objectui 4016370a read 'Draft discarded: QA Widget' — a regression row, expected PASS (objectstack-ai/objectui#12690, closed by objectui PR #12830, 0f42aaf8, in the console pin 4016370a and on objectui main; ResourceEditPage.tsx falls back to type/name only for an item with no label)

FIXED, regression row, expected PASS (objectui#11816): leaving an inline editor with no value change no longer reads '1 row modified · Save All (1)' (QA run #23163 at objectui 1fb1ced36243; pin data-table-noop-edit-11816.test.tsx) — negative[1]

Undo is scored only where a surface offers it, and on stock ONE surface does: the import. An import run as a job (the wizard's 'runs as an undoable job' option) is listed in the import history with 'Undo import', which deletes the records it created and restores the records it updated to their previous values; QA run #25817 at 6679644a read it working in both create and update modes. Elsewhere no stock surface offers Undo: only an action declaring `undoable` pushes an Undo op (inline and form edits push none), and the showcase declares no undoable action (records-forms.record-edit-undo, blocked(fixture)). So acceptance[5] is scored on the import variant. Undo's absence elsewhere is recorded in the evidence and is never a FAIL of this item: which writes should offer Undo is a product decision, not this item's oracle

variants: record create — New form save on showcase_task

record inline edit — on the task object's Grid view (the named view `grid`, labelled 'Grid': the one task list that declares inlineEdit: true, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/task.view.ts; the default All Tasks list declares none), double-click a Priority cell (the grid has no 'Edit inline' button), change it, then Save row or Save All
bulk delete — select two rows → Delete in the selection bar → confirm

kanban move — drag a card Backlog → To Do (direct manipulation: the card in its new column IS the success feedback; a move the transition rule blocks never leaves the client — its lane is dimmed, data-kanban-drop-blocked, and the drop sends nothing, #25933)

declared record action — Mark Done on a task record (declared successMessage `{{ record.title | default:'Task' }} marked done.`, which names the task, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#MarkDoneAction)
param action dialog — Setup → Users → Invite User → Confirm (declared successMessage `Invitation sent to {{ result.email }}`)

approval decision — open the request from the approvals page, /_console/apps/com.example.showcase/system/approvals (the 'Approvals inbox' link opens the review-queue page, which is not where the decision is taken). The route has no drawer: opening a request navigates to its record page (sys_approval_request_detail), where the decision is taken → Approve with a comment
import — Tasks → Import a two-row CSV → the result screen
Studio autosave — rename a field label in the scratch package
Studio publish — Publish the scratch package

Studio discard — on the metadata designer (/_console/apps/setup/metadata/object/OBJ for a scratch-package object with a pending draft), click 'Discard draft' and accept the in-app confirm dialog (it is no longer the browser's native confirm); the Studio pillars offer no discard. A scratch object's name carries its package's namespace prefix, so read it off the package before building the URL
settings save — Settings → Localization → save a value
steps: sign in as admin; keep a second context (or the REST API) open to read server truth independently of the UI

for each variant perform the write once, then within ~2 s capture a screenshot and the DOM of every feedback region — toasts ([data-sonner-toast]), role=status / role=alert regions, and the surface's own save indicator — recording the verbatim text, or its absence
for each variant read server-side whether the write landed (GET the record, the metadata item or the sys_ row) and record the request's status from the network log

repeat the record rows signed in as the member persona, on member-owned records — the stock member's set (showcase_member_default) grants showcase_task read + create only, and the console applies it up front: it offers the member no inline edit, no row selection and no kanban drag, so those three rows cannot be driven as the member (record them as not offered, never as refused). The member's create row runs; for the refusal row use the member's Mark Done on a task record, which answers 403 PERMISSION_DENIED (its error feedback is clause 3's to score). To drive the edit rows as a member, bind the member to the contributor position (showcase_contributor grants task edit, not delete)

negative pass: (a) submit the create form with a required field empty; then break a validation rule — showcase_task's only rule is the UPDATE-time state machine task_status_flow (no create-time rule exists), so drive it as a refused transition, Backlog → Done, through the API: PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_task/ID {status: 'done'} on a backlog task answers 400, with the rule's invalid_transition refusal and its message 'Invalid task status transition.' (packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts). Record that request's status and error code for acceptance[3]. No console surface can send that write. The record form's status select and the grid's inline editor offer only the values the machine admits from the stored state (ui/packages/plugin-form/src/stateMachineOptions.ts, and plugin-grid through stateMachineNextValues), so Done is not offered from Backlog. Record the narrowed picker as those surfaces' answer, as with the kanban's dimmed lane. ⛔ Not the kanban: the drop gate (#25933, ui/packages/plugin-kanban/src/KanbanImpl.tsx) dims a lane the transition rule blocks (data-kanban-drop-blocked) and a drop there sends no request, so no refusal reaches the server; record the dimmed lane as that surface's answer; (b) open an inline editor and leave it without changing the value

where a variant offers Undo, click it and read the record back — on stock the import does (knownGaps[3]): run the two-row CSV import as a job, once creating and once updating, then 'Undo import' from the import history — it asks through the browser's native window.confirm (ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx), unlike Studio discard's in-app dialog, so a driver accepts it as a dialog event — and read the rows back

acceptance.clause: every write that landed server-side produced visible feedback on the surface that started it — a toast, an inline status, or (direct manipulation only) the item visibly in its new place
acceptance.verify: per variant, the captured feedback text is non-empty, or (kanban only) the card's column in the DOM matches the status the server read returns; pair every row with its step-3 server read. The Studio top bar's save status ('Saved' / 「已保存」, with or without a time) is not write feedback under this convention and does not count here: a Studio row whose only feedback is that status scores FAIL
acceptance.evidence: per-variant table: variant · landed (y/n, request status) · feedback text verbatim or 'none' · screenshot

acceptance.clause: success feedback names its subject: a record-level write names the record or item (its title, label or display name) or the count; a singleton page (settings) and a named automation (e.g. Flow "X" completed) are their own subject and pass as they are; a bare 'Success' / 'Done' or a machine name never passes
acceptance.verify: two steps per row. First classify the write: record-level (a record create, edit or delete, the import, the approval decision, a record or param action, a Studio item) or singleton / named automation (the settings save, a named Flow run). Then score it by that class's test. Record-level: PASS when the captured text names the record or item (record title or display name, invitee email, package or item label, e.g. 'Approved "EXP-2001"') or the count ('N created · M skipped', '1 row saved'); text that names only the object ('Task created successfully') scores FAIL — the console's record create and edit toasts read that way until #26172 (the dialog paths) and #26461 (the full-page /new and /edit form route) — both closed fixed, so those rows are now expected PASS, and a toast naming only the object is a regression. Singleton / named automation: PASS when the text names that page or automation ('Settings saved', 'Flow "Reassign Task" completed'). In either class a generic 'Done' / 'Success' or a raw snake_case name scores FAIL for that row. The Studio top bar's save status ('Saved' / 「已保存」, with or without a time) names no item, so it is not write feedback under this convention: a Studio row (autosave, publish, discard) passes only on a toast or inline text that names the item or package, and a row whose only feedback is that status scores FAIL

acceptance.clause: a declared successMessage is the text the user sees
acceptance.verify: for Mark Done and Invite User compare the toast text with the action's declared successMessage (examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#MarkDoneAction, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts#invite_user)
acceptance.evidence: declared string vs shown string, per action

acceptance.clause: a refused write shows an error that says why — next to the field or in an error toast — and never a success message
acceptance.verify: negative (a) has two legitimate refusal shapes, and the evidence records which one occurred: the request answers 4xx and the UI shows the server's reason; or the console blocks the submit itself — no write request leaves the browser — and shows the reason at the field (e.g. 'Title is required') or in an error toast (QA run #23953 met this shape for the required-field case). Either way no success toast appears in the same capture window. A write request answering 2xx, a refusal that shows no reason, or any success feedback is a FAIL
acceptance.evidence: request status and error code, the error text shown, screenshot

acceptance.clause: a no-op claims nothing — leaving an editor unchanged produces no saved/modified state and sends no write
acceptance.verify: negative (b): no PATCH/PUT in the network log and no modified or saved indicator in the DOM
acceptance.evidence: network log excerpt and DOM capture

acceptance.clause: where Undo is offered it restores the prior value server-side
acceptance.verify: after Undo, GET the record and compare the field with its pre-edit value. On stock the import is the surface that offers it (knownGaps[3]): after 'Undo import' the rows a create-mode import wrote are gone and the rows an update-mode import changed carry their pre-import values

negative: a refused write (required field empty, validation rule broken) never shows a success toast
a no-op (open and close an inline editor without a change) produces no 'modified' state and no write request
feedback claiming success while the write did not land (4xx/5xx, or no request at all) is a FAIL — the inverse of a silent success

items.title: Every disabled control explains itself — the reason shows on hover and on keyboard focus, and is exposed as an accessible description
personas: member (non-admin) — for the disabled states only a non-privileged persona meets

requires: a showcase_task record with done = false (the stock seeds carry several)
the read-only showcase package in Studio (stock)
knownGaps: FIXED, now the calibration reference (objectui#11811): the task record's Archive button (examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#ArchiveTaskAction, disabled while has(record.done) && record.done != true) carries its reason as a tooltip AND an aria-describedby on a focusable wrapper, in both its record_header and record_section placements (objectui DeclaredActionsBar.tsx; pin DeclaredActionsBar.disabledReason-11811.test.tsx). The action spec has no author-facing reason next to `disabled`, so the reason is the generic platform fallback — record it as generic under clause 3. Check this control first to calibrate both the hover and the keyboard oracle

Studio's Publish button on the read-only showcase package and the import wizard's disabled Next are FIXED for the keyboard (QA run #23953 at objectui daeb77fc84dd): each carries its reason on a focusable wrapper with an aria-describedby, so both now calibrate hover AND keyboard, expected PASS; Studio's automation Enabled toggle and the field inspector's Remove pass the same way. Regression rows, expected PASS since QA run #24570 (objectui 4016370a, two fresh loads each): the field inspector's read-only Label / API name / Type / Required / Move up-down sit in a focusable panel wrapper described by the read-only reason, with the tooltip on focus (objectstack-ai/objectui#12303, closed by objectui PR #12324, b64fda3f — the rail body described by fieldRailReasonId, StudioDesignSurface.tsx); and the Studio validation editor's body on a read-only package is a role=group tab stop described by the reason, with the tooltip on hover and focus (objectstack-ai/objectui#12691, closed by objectui PR #12833, d0a00d79, ObjectValidationsPanel.tsx). Both fixes are in the console pin 4016370a and on objectui main

variants: declared action disabled by its `disabled` predicate — Archive on a not-done task, record header AND record section placement
Studio Publish on a read-only package
Studio controls on a read-only package — the automation enable toggle, field inspector inputs, validation editor selects
import wizard — the step's continue/import button while a required field is unmapped
a form submit button, where the surface disables it instead of validating on submit
toolbar or bulk buttons rendered disabled for the member persona
steps: sign in as admin; on each variant locate every control rendered disabled (the disabled attribute, aria-disabled=true, or data-disabled)
hover each one for 1 s and screenshot; then reach it — or its focusable wrapper — with Tab and screenshot again
read the accessibility tree for each control: accessible name, accessible description (the aria-describedby target's text) and title
repeat the member-persona variant signed in as a member

acceptance.clause: every disabled control shows a reason on pointer hover
acceptance.verify: the hover screenshot shows a tooltip or adjacent text explaining the disabled state; nothing appearing scores FAIL for that control
acceptance.evidence: per-control screenshot with the control's label

acceptance.clause: the same reason is reachable without a pointer and exposed to assistive technology
acceptance.verify: the control or its focusable wrapper is in the tab order and carries an accessible description (aria-describedby resolving to non-empty text) or a title; a disabled control with neither scores FAIL

acceptance.clause: the reason is specific when the author or the platform knows the condition, generic only as a fallback
acceptance.verify: classify each reason: one that names the condition (e.g. 'Available once the task is done', 'This package is read-only') or a generic fallback ('Not available') passes, and the evidence records which of the two it was; an empty reason fails
acceptance.evidence: verbatim reason strings, classified specific / generic / none

negative: an ENABLED control carries no leftover disabled reason
a control removed by its `visible` predicate is absent from the DOM rather than rendered disabled — out of this item's scope; record it if seen

items.title: Where a label exists users see the label — machine names, raw ids and spec paths appear only as secondary text

steps: before the browser: for each variant read the served metadata (GET /api/v1/meta/<type>/<name>) and note each sampled item's label next to its machine name — expectations derive from data
sign in as admin; visit each variant, screenshot it and capture the DOM text of each sampled item's primary label

scan the visible text of every variant for an id-shaped string (20+ alphanumeric characters), a dotted Zod path (segment.index.segment), a TypeScript class name, or an issue reference (repo#number)

acceptance.clause: the primary text of each sampled item is its label, not its machine name
acceptance.verify: compare the rendered primary text with the label and name read in step 1; rendered text equal to the name while a distinct label exists scores FAIL for that row
acceptance.evidence: per-row table: surface · label · name · rendered text

acceptance.clause: user references render as a person, never as an id
acceptance.verify: the rendered text equals the user's name or email from the sys_user read; an id-shaped string scores FAIL
acceptance.evidence: rendered string vs sys_user name / email

acceptance.clause: where a machine name is shown it is secondary — beside its label and visually subordinate
acceptance.verify: the machine name appears only next to its label, in smaller, muted or monospace text
acceptance.evidence: a screenshot per row where a machine name appears

acceptance.clause: user-facing banners and help text carry no raw spec path, class name or tracker id
acceptance.verify: no visible string on any variant matches a dotted Zod path, a TypeScript class name such as MetadataClient, or an issue reference (repo#number, or a bare #NNNN). Score a match by who wrote the text: inside text the PLATFORM builds — a renderer banner, or server-built prose such as Explain's evaluation pipeline — it FAILS; inside text the APP's author wrote (a label, description or flow label carrying a tracker reference) it is an authoring finding, recorded with its surface and scored like negative[0], never a renderer FAIL. An ADR number cited in server-built prose (ADR-NNNN) is not an issue reference: record each one with its surface, and do not score it
acceptance.evidence: every matching string, with its surface

negative: a machine name rendered because the item genuinely declares no label is an authoring gap, not a renderer FAIL — read the metadata before scoring
developer surfaces (the API panel, Advanced JSON editors) may show machine names — out of scope
